# Release Workflow Overview

This project uses automated semantic versioning while respecting protected branch rules.

---

## CI (`ci.yml`)

### CI Triggers

- Pull requests
- Pushes to any branch

### CI Responsibilities

- Analyze and format check (flutter analyze, dart format)
- Validate commit messages (conventional commits)
- Run **semantic-release in dry-run mode** (preview only)

No versions, tags, or releases are created here.

---

## Semantic Release (`semantic-release.yml`)

### Semantic Release Trigger

After CI succeeds on `main`.

### Semantic Release Responsibilities

- Analyze commits since the last release
- Determine the next semantic version
- Write that version into `manabi_do/pubspec.yaml` and commit it back to `main`
  as `chore(release): X.Y.Z [skip ci]` (the `[skip ci]` prevents a release loop)
- Create:
  - A Git tag (`vX.Y.Z`), pointing at that bump commit
  - A GitHub Release with autogenerated notes

This step defines the **official released version**.

Keeping `pubspec.yaml` in sync matters because the Settings screen reads the
version from `PackageInfo.fromPlatform()`. Without the bump, every build that
does not go through `build-android.yml` — local `flutter run`, the widgetbook
web build — reports whatever stale version `pubspec.yaml` happens to hold.

The bump commit is pushed straight to `main`, which the branch ruleset would
normally reject; this works because `RELEASE_PAT` belongs to an admin, and the
ruleset grants the admin role an unconditional bypass.

---

## Build Artifacts (`build-android.yml`)

### Artifact Build Trigger

When a GitHub Release is published.

### Artifact Build Responsibilities

- Set up Flutter and Java
- Decode the release keystore from secrets
- Re-derive the version from the release tag and stamp it into `pubspec.yaml`,
  along with the workflow run number as the build number (`versionCode`). The
  version is redundant with the bump commit above and stays as a safeguard: it
  keeps the artifact correct even if the bump commit never lands, and the run
  number is what guarantees a strictly increasing `versionCode` for Play.
- Build the signed Android App Bundle (AAB)
- Upload the AAB to the GitHub Release
- Deploy the AAB to the Play Store internal track via Fastlane

Guarantees artifacts are signed, versioned, and available on the internal track without manual upload.

---

## GitHub Pages (`pages.yml`)

### Pages Trigger

Pushes to `main` that modify the `docs/` directory.

### Pages Responsibilities

- Deploy the `docs/` folder to GitHub Pages
- Serves the privacy policy at `https://mirai-toto.github.io/manabi-do/privacy/`

---

## Full Flow

1. A feature/fix branch is merged into `main`
2. CI runs and passes
3. Semantic Release:
   - Calculates next version
   - Bumps `pubspec.yaml` and pushes the bump commit to `main`
   - Creates Git tag and GitHub Release
4. The new release triggers the Android build workflow
5. The signed AAB is attached to the GitHub Release
6. The AAB is manually uploaded to the Play Console

---

## Key Principle

**Releases define versions. CI deploys to internal track. Humans promote to production.**

Automation handles versioning, tagging, building, and Play Store internal track deployment. Promotion to production remains a manual step.
